name: Learn: Build, Save & Push Images
objective: CKAD › Application Design and Build (20%). Goal: build a container image from a Dockerfile, modify/tag it, save it to a tarball, make it available to the cluster, and push it to a registry — the image-lifecycle tasks the exam expects.
description: Build an image on the host, label it, export it as a .tgz, load it into the kind cluster and run it, then push it to a local registry. Everything runs against your host Docker + the kindlab cluster.

questions.title: Build an image from a Dockerfile
questions.teach:
Container images are built from a **Dockerfile** (a.k.a. Containerfile) plus a **build context** — the directory handed to the builder.

**Build commands:**
- `docker build -t name:tag <context>` — build and tag; add `-f path/Dockerfile` to point at a non-default file.
- Exam/rootless tools are interchangeable: `podman build -t name:tag .` and `buildah bud -t name:tag .` take the same flags (CKAD/CKS environments often ship podman, not docker).
- `--build-arg KEY=val` feeds a Dockerfile `ARG`; `--label k=v` stamps a label without editing the file; `--target <stage>` stops at a named stage in a multi-stage build.

**Dockerfile essentials:** `FROM` base · `COPY`/`ADD` files in · `RUN` build steps (each instruction is a cached layer) · `ENV`/`ARG` · `WORKDIR` · `USER` (run non-root) · `EXPOSE` (documentation only) · `ENTRYPOINT` (the fixed executable) vs `CMD` (default args).

**Gotchas:**
- The context is tarred and shipped to the daemon — a huge context or a missing `.dockerignore` makes builds crawl; `.` means the *current* dir, not the Dockerfile's dir.
- Order instructions least- to most-frequently-changed to reuse layer cache.
- `CMD` exec form `["sh","-c","…"]` vs shell form changes PID 1 / signal handling.
- Always `-t` a build; an untagged image is `<none>:<none>` (dangling).
questions.prompt:
A build context is prepared at `/tmp/kindlab-img` (a `Dockerfile` + `hello.txt`). Build an image tagged `myapp:1.0` from it.

Target: `docker image inspect myapp:1.0` succeeds and the image carries the Dockerfile's `LABEL stage=base`.
questions.hint: `docker build -t myapp:1.0 /tmp/kindlab-img` — then `docker image inspect myapp:1.0` to confirm it exists.
questions.solution:
docker build -t myapp:1.0 /tmp/kindlab-img
docker image inspect myapp:1.0 --format '{{ index .Config.Labels "stage" }}'   # base

verification.description: image myapp:1.0 built from the provided Dockerfile

questions.title: Modify the image: add a label and tag
questions.teach:
The same context can produce many images; you **modify** an image by changing the Dockerfile and rebuilding, or by stamping metadata at build time.

**Relabel / retag without editing the Dockerfile:**
- `docker build -t myapp:2.0 --label version=2 <context>` — adds/overrides an image label.
- `docker tag src:tag new:tag` — a second name for the **same** image id (no rebuild); this is how you prepare a registry path like `registry/repo:tag`.
- `docker image inspect name:tag` shows `.Config.Labels`, `.Config.Cmd`, layers; `docker history name:tag` shows each layer.

**Gotchas:**
- A tag is just a pointer — `docker tag` makes another name, it does not copy or rebuild.
- `--label` lands under `.Config.Labels` (same place a Dockerfile `LABEL` does, but without baking a new layer).
- Rebuilding with an existing tag moves the tag to the new image and leaves the old one dangling.
- Image **digests** (`name@sha256:…`) are immutable; tags are mutable — pin digests for supply-chain safety (CKS).
questions.prompt:
Rebuild the same context as `myapp:2.0`, adding an image label `version=2` **via the build flag** (don't edit the Dockerfile).

Target: image `myapp:2.0` exists and its config label `version` equals `2`.
questions.hint: `docker build -t myapp:2.0 --label version=2 /tmp/kindlab-img`. Verify: `docker image inspect myapp:2.0 --format '{{ index .Config.Labels "version" }}'`.
questions.solution:
docker build -t myapp:2.0 --label version=2 /tmp/kindlab-img
docker image inspect myapp:2.0 --format '{{ index .Config.Labels "version" }}'   # 2

verification.description: image myapp:2.0 built with label version=2

questions.title: Save the image to a .tgz tarball
questions.teach:
Images move between machines as a **tarball** without needing a registry.

**Save vs export (know the difference):**
- `docker save name:tag -o out.tar` (or `| gzip > out.tgz`) — saves the **image** with all layers + metadata; reload with `docker load -i out.tgz`.
- `docker export <container> -o fs.tar` — exports a **container's flat filesystem** (no layers/history); reload with `docker import`.
- podman: `podman save` / `podman load` are the equivalents.

**Gotchas:**
- `save`/`load` preserve tags, layers and config; `export`/`import` flatten and **lose** CMD/ENV/history unless you re-specify them.
- `docker save` writes an **uncompressed** tar by default — pipe through `gzip` to get a genuine `.tgz` (naming a plain tar `.tgz` doesn't compress it).
- A docker-save archive contains `manifest.json` + per-layer blobs — that's how tools recognise it.
- Move the file (scp/cp), then `docker load` on the far side — no registry round-trip.
questions.prompt:
Save the `myapp:2.0` image to a gzipped tarball at `/tmp/kindlab-img/myapp-2.0.tgz`.

Target: the file exists and is a valid docker image archive (contains `manifest.json`).
questions.hint: `docker save myapp:2.0 | gzip > /tmp/kindlab-img/myapp-2.0.tgz`. Check it: `tar -tzf /tmp/kindlab-img/myapp-2.0.tgz | grep manifest.json`.
questions.solution:
docker save myapp:2.0 | gzip > /tmp/kindlab-img/myapp-2.0.tgz
tar -tzf /tmp/kindlab-img/myapp-2.0.tgz | grep manifest.json   # present

verification.description: myapp:2.0 saved to a valid gzipped image archive

questions.title: Load the image into the cluster and run it
questions.teach:
A locally-built image isn't visible to the cluster until it's on the nodes — kind nodes run their **own** containerd image store, separate from your host Docker.

**Get a local image onto kind nodes:**
- `kind load docker-image name:tag --name <cluster>` — copies a host image into every node.
- `kind load image-archive out.tgz --name <cluster>` — loads from a `docker save` archive.
- (Or push to a wired-in local **registry** and pull by `localhost:5001/name:tag` — the next step.)

**Run it:** set `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` (or `Never`) so the kubelet uses the on-node image instead of trying to pull from a registry.

**Gotchas:**
- Default `imagePullPolicy` is `Always` for the `:latest` tag and `IfNotPresent` otherwise — a `:latest` local image can still trigger a failing pull; set it explicitly.
- `ErrImagePull`/`ImagePullBackOff` on a local image means you didn't `kind load` it (or the name/tag doesn't match).
- `kind load` must target the right `--name`; loading into the wrong cluster leaves the pod unable to find the image.
- Every node has its own store — `kind load` covers all nodes for you.
questions.prompt:
Make `myapp:2.0` available to the `kindlab` cluster, then in namespace `images-learn` run a pod named `myapp` using it, with `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`.

Target: pod `myapp` in `images-learn` is `Running` using image `myapp:2.0`.
questions.hint: `kind load docker-image myapp:2.0 --name kindlab`, then `kubectl -n images-learn run myapp --image=myapp:2.0 --image-pull-policy=IfNotPresent`.
questions.solution:
kind load docker-image myapp:2.0 --name kindlab
kubectl -n images-learn run myapp --image=myapp:2.0 --image-pull-policy=IfNotPresent
kubectl -n images-learn get pod myapp -o wide

verification.description: pod myapp is Running from the local image myapp:2.0

questions.title: Push the image to a registry
questions.teach:
A **registry** is the shared store pods pull from. The flow is tag → push → (cluster) pull.

**Push:**
- `docker tag name:tag <registry>/<repo>:tag` then `docker push <registry>/<repo>:tag`.
- `localhost:5001` here is a plain-HTTP local registry (Docker treats `localhost` as insecure-allowed); real registries need `docker login` first — that writes `~/.docker/config.json`, which becomes a `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` **imagePullSecret**.
- Inspect a registry over its HTTP API: `GET /v2/_catalog` (repos) and `GET /v2/<repo>/tags/list`.

**Gotchas:**
- The image **name must embed the registry host** to push there — `docker push myapp:2.0` goes to Docker Hub; it must be `localhost:5001/myapp:2.0`.
- Private registries need an **imagePullSecret** on the pod/ServiceAccount or pulls fail `401`.
- A non-`localhost` insecure registry needs daemon `insecure-registries` config or a trusted TLS cert.
- Pin by **digest** (`@sha256:`) in production/CKS so a mutable tag can't be swapped under you.
questions.prompt:
A local registry runs at `localhost:5001`. Tag `myapp:2.0` as `localhost:5001/myapp:2.0` and push it.

Target: the registry's catalog lists repo `myapp` with tag `2.0`.
questions.hint: `docker tag myapp:2.0 localhost:5001/myapp:2.0` then `docker push localhost:5001/myapp:2.0`. Confirm: `curl -s localhost:5001/v2/_catalog` and `curl -s localhost:5001/v2/myapp/tags/list`.

verification.description: myapp:2.0 pushed to the local registry (catalog + tag)
